questions.question: An if-statement can be used to execute a block of code only when a certain condition is true.
The condition inside an if-statement must always evaluate to a boolean value (True or False).
An if-statement without an else block is not allowed in Python.
You can use the '==' operator in an if-statement to check for equality between two values.
In Python, 'elif' is used to check an additional condition if the previous if-statement condition is True.
An if-statement can contain multiple elif blocks to check different conditions in sequence.
It is possible to nest an if-statement inside another if-statement to create more complex decision structures.
Using indentation incorrectly in an if-statement will not affect the execution of the program.
Using logical operators like 'and' or 'or' in the condition of an if-statement can allow you to combine multiple conditions.
The 'else' block of an if-else structure is mandatory and must appear after the 'if' block.
